name: Panel
summary: Use a panel to highlight the outcome of an important action, especially successful completion of a transaction.
whenToUse: Use at the top of a confirmation page to tell users that they completed an important action.
Include a reference number or other short result in the body when users must retain it.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a panel for routine information, warnings or validation errors.
Do not rely on the panel as the entire confirmation page; follow it with what happens next.

anatomy.name: Confirmation panel
anatomy.description: A govuk-panel govuk-panel--confirmation container carries the highlighted outcome.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: A concise heading states the successful result and is normally the page h1.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: Optional content shows a reference or another immediately important detail.

variants.name: Confirmation
variants.use: The primary outcome at the start of a confirmation page.

behaviour: No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
Render the panel after the server has completed or authoritatively confirmed the action, not as an optimistic client-only state.
Follow the panel with details about next steps, timing, records and support.
accessibility: Use an h1 for the confirmation title when it is the page's main heading.
Ensure the result is explicit in text and not conveyed only by the green background.
When navigation moves to the confirmation page, make the page title and heading identify the completed task.
content: State the outcome directly, such as “Application complete”.
Label any reference number and make it easy to copy accurately.
Do not use celebratory or vague copy that obscures what was completed.
